title: Canyon front door (seam 3)
description: GET and PUT /api/v1/front-door: how people reach apps on a Kubernetes host. contracts/routes.md (Platform, the front-door row) is canonical; this schema pins the shape. The answer is /run's front_door (contracts/executor.md, On Kubernetes) field for field, without the sign-in client's secret, which is written and never answered. The golden under contracts/testdata/front-door/ is one save told end to end: the body, the refusal a probe answered while the certificate did not cover the form, the answer once it did, and the address a deploy records under it; then the same host's door saved unprobed while a platform webhook is saved, the probe having failed (#2438).

probed.description: Whether the save that stored this door passed the probe (enforced and ok). Canyon runs no app behind a door that has not; only a choice 1, saved while a platform webhook or a deploy repo is saved, is ever stored without, or a door whose probed a probe_failed refusal on NetworkPolicy cleared (#2507).

enforcing.description: Whether the save that stored this door found NetworkPolicy enforced, whatever the certificate (routes.md, the front-door row; #2507). Nothing builds behind a door that is not, under either run_by.

grants_note.description: Whether a grant to a person applies through the stored front door (routes.md, the front-door row): the experience design's other-issuer line, its alb line, or empty.
enum: People sign in at this front door through another issuer than Canyon's, so an app shared with a person won't let them in. Sharing with a group or with everyone still does.
An app shared with a person lets them in only if the load balancer signs people in through Canyon's own sign-in. Sharing with a group or with everyone works either way.

egress_note.description: Whether apps routed through Canyon can reach the stored front door's sign-in (routes.md, the front-door row): the experience design's gateway-sign-in line, or empty.
enum: Apps routed through Canyon can't reach a sign-in served through this cluster's own gateway, so nobody can sign in to them. Use another sign-in provider here, or turn off Through Canyon in Settings › Outbound.

discovery_note.description: Whether Canyon has recorded the stored choice 2 front door's discovery (routes.md, the front-door row): the experience design's discovery line while it has not, or empty.
enum: Canyon couldn't read your sign-in provider's discovery document yet and keeps trying every minute; until it does, apps whose outbound mode is allowlist can't sign people in.

probe_note.description: While the stored front door is not enforcing, the experience design's not-enforcing line; else while it is not probed, its not-checked line (routes.md, the front-door row); either then one space and why (the probe's fix, or the probe_unavailable sentence), or the line alone for a door stored before the field; empty otherwise.
probe_note.pattern: ^$|^Not checked on this cluster: (your platform can run apps behind this front door, but Canyon won't until a save passes the check|Canyon builds nothing here until a save finds NetworkPolicy enforced, so no deploy goes through, whoever runs the apps)\.( .+)?$

probe_result.description: contracts/executor.md, POST /probe: what the save asked before writing.
